# Home

<!-- Generated from in-app Help; do not edit by hand. -->

What needs the coordinator now, across every ward, ED and movement.

## What is on the screen

1. Bed flow right now. Open movements, Ready beds and the share in use across the network. Press Open movements or Ready for its breakdown.
2. How full the network is. The share of network beds in use, with At risk once it passes the line. Open it for Capacity.
3. What needs you. How many need you now, split into act now and to decide. Show act now takes you to that list.
4. Checking. Bed counts gone stale, wards not reporting and outage packs never printed. Open a part to see which.
5. Quick controls. The tools you use most, such as Ward updates and Find a bed. Each opens in the Tools panel on this page.
6. Every ED at a glance. One tile per emergency department, with how many are waiting and the longest wait. Choose a tile to narrow the list to that ED, and again to clear it.
7. Needs you and Flow. Needs you is what needs a person. Flow lists every open movement, and its tabs narrow it by stage. On a phone, Later today is the third list.
8. More. Today's review, Night view and Alerts history.
9. Since the last shift. What changed since the previous shift started. Review opens the changes to go through.
10. Needs you. Act now first, then referrals to decide and what you are waiting on others for. A row for someone waiting for a bed opens their placement checks; other rows open the record they are about. A person always chooses the bed.
11. Ward calls. The wards to ring about waiting referrals, in call order, to read or print.
12. Beds that fit. For each bed type, beds against the people waiting, now and tomorrow. Short means more people than beds. Counts only.
13. Later today. Planned moves and expected times for the rest of your shift and after it, from times the records hold. Past planned time comes first.
14. Tomorrow. Expected and confirmed discharges and planned admissions for tomorrow.

In BedChart, open Help and choose Show me around this screen to see each part lit in turn.

_Prototype on synthetic data. Not for real patients._
